claim_ceiling: SYNTHETIC_TEST_ONLY; no actual labour-market estimate, job count, worker profile, shortage, or causal claim

source.provenance_note: Invented value constructed to test supply counts; not sourced from a real registry.

measure.denominator: people registered in the simulated system
measure.definition: Artificial count of registrations in a toy evidence source.

uncertainty.method_note: Deliberately artificial bounds; not a statistical interval.

freshness.reason: Synthetic source timestamp is in the fixture's reference period.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: Artificial crosswalk; cannot imply equivalence to a real occupation.

evidence_limits: This number cannot establish task-ready capacity or an occupational shortage.

source.provenance_note: Models a high-demand-list marker without claiming an official list entry.

measure.denominator: occupation entries in the synthetic reference list
measure.definition: Artificial marker simulating that an occupation appears on a demand planning list.

uncertainty.method_note: Deterministic fixture value, not a probability.

freshness.reason: The value is an invented test flag, not a periodically refreshed observation.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: No real taxonomy code or occupation is represented.

evidence_limits: A high-demand planning flag is not a shortage label.
This record must not be used for recruitment or foreign-worker decisions.

source.provenance_note: Invented count of advertisements; deliberate duplicate and funding trap.

measure.denominator: deduplicated ads have not yet been established
measure.definition: Artificial count before deduplication and funded-vacancy validation.

uncertainty.method_note: Range is artificial and expresses potential duplicate sensitivity, not a confidence interval.

freshness.reason: No authoritative closure/cancellation signal is present in this simulated source.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: Advert labels deliberately do not reliably identify required task scope.

evidence_limits: Advertisements do not prove an approved budget or payer.
Duplicate rows and stale openings may inflate apparent demand.
No shortage inference is permitted from this record alone.

source.provenance_note: Simulates externally verified, approved work orders in an artificial example.

measure.denominator: approved and funded vacancies with an identified payer
measure.definition: Artificial count that is funded within this test case; no real payer is asserted.

uncertainty.method_note: Fixture assumes the payer evidence is complete for testing gate semantics.

freshness.reason: Synthetic approval record is dated to the reference date.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: Exact only within the artificial test ontology.

evidence_limits: Even funded vacancies do not prove worker scarcity or durable job creation.

source.provenance_note: Invented count of people who passed a task-specific supervised practical assessment.

measure.denominator: participants assessed against the exact task profile
measure.definition: Artificial number of people whose observed practical assessment meets the defined task profile.

uncertainty.method_note: Artificial sensitivity range, not a sampling interval.

freshness.reason: Synthetic assessment date matches the reference window.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: Exact only inside the artificial test profile.

evidence_limits: Does not establish availability, willingness, licence scope or geographic accessibility.

source.provenance_note: Invented offer-decline rate used to test job-quality confounding.

measure.denominator: documented offers in the synthetic cohort
measure.definition: Artificial share of offers declined where pay, shift, safety and travel may be nonviable.

uncertainty.method_note: Artificial range used as a stress interval, not a confidence interval.

freshness.reason: Artificial observation window ends on the fixture date.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: The metric measures offer conditions, not occupation mapping.

evidence_limits: Declines do not uniquely identify a cause without candidate and job-condition evidence.
This must not be interpreted as an individual willingness/risk score.

source.provenance_note: Artificial service queue with duplicates and unapproved items.

measure.definition: Artificial reported count before duplicate detection, approval, funding checks and verification.

uncertainty.method_note: Artificial range illustrates how duplicate/invalid reports can distort the denominator.

freshness.reason: No independently verified current queue snapshot is assumed.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: A report code may not correspond one-to-one to a distinct job or occupational skill.

evidence_limits: Backlog rows are not necessarily distinct valid jobs.
A queue count is not proof of a skills shortage or funded demand.

source.provenance_note: Invented cohort transition counts designed to prevent training completion being confused with employment impact.

measure.definition: Artificial number of learners finishing a course; paid-placement and retention outcomes are separate measures.

uncertainty.method_note: Deterministic invented count, not a statistical estimate.

taxonomy.crosswalk_note: A course label alone does not establish task-level equivalence.

evidence_limits: Training completion does not establish practical competence, paid placement, earnings or retention.
Do not describe this record as jobs created.
